ai.title: Add test budget and global state guidance to docs/testing.md
ai.summary: docs/testing.md adds guidance on machine-global test subjects and polling helper budgets. Explains that `orphan-reaper` tests require atomic `mkdir` locks due to shared process table state. Introduces `test/support/budgets.ts` to enforce that `waitFor` deadlines remain shorter than test budgets, preventing unattributed unhandled errors.

eli5.text: If a test relies on a process running on your machine rather than something isolated, two copies of it can interfere with each other by trying to manage the same global set of processes. To prevent this, an atomic directory-creation lock is now used to ensure only one such test runs at a time. Additionally, test files now explicitly declare how long they expect to take, and polling helpers are checked to give up before that deadline. This change is live today and affects how tests behave on shared or heavily loaded machines by making failures more attributable and preventing unattributed unhandled errors from masking the real issue.

ai.title: docs: update CI flake handling for unit vs integration suites
ai.summary: Updated `docs/testing.md` to clarify that unit suites now fail on retry, while integration suites only generate a `Flaky suite` warning. This change reflects measured CI data where retries rescued integration tests (Postgres containers) but never unit logic, enforcing stricter flake detection for unit tests. The documentation also notes that `max_attempts` remains 3 for unit tests to distinguish flaky from broken suites, and emphasizes that CI runners do not apply resource contention.

eli5.text: When a test in the main code-checking system fails and then passes on a retry, the system treats it differently now. For the core unit checks (the fast ones that test specific pieces of logic), a pass only on the second or third try now fails the whole submission, because analysis showed retries never actually helped these, they just hide real problems. For the slower integration checks (the ones that test multiple parts together, like database connections), a retry rescue still works but leaves a warning note for people to investigate. Right now, if you see a test pass only after retrying in the unit category, you should know it's flaky and needs fixing.

ai.title: GPT-5.6 cache-aware step prompt placement
ai.summary: A new `ephemeralTrailingMessageBreaksCache` gate in `common/src/constants/model-config.ts` returns true for `gpt-5.6` models, whose OpenAI prompt cache is destroyed when a trailing message is deleted on the next step. When the gate is true, `run-agent-step.ts` stops appending a per-step ephemeral step prompt and instead places a single resident STEP_PROMPT once at the turn's start via `loopAgentSteps`; for all other models only the ephemeral form is appended per step as before. The shared `stepPromptMessage` builder in `util/messages.ts` distinguishes the two forms by omitting `timeToLive` for resident prompts and keeping `timeToLive: 'agentStep'` for ephemeral ones. `agents/context-pruner.ts` was updated alongside to carry a resident STEP_PROMPT through summarization instead of dropping it. The change keeps GPT-5.6 history append-only so its prefix cache stays warm, at the cost of one extra persistent system-style message per turn for those models only.

ai.title: Fix Windows tar path in self-update test script
ai.summary: The `cli/scripts/test-published-self-update.ts` script now explicitly resolves the path to Windows' native `bsdtar` (`System32\tar.exe`) instead of relying on the generic `tar` command. This change prevents Git Bash's GNU `tar` from misinterpreting Windows paths as obsolete remote tape addresses during archive extraction. The fix applies only to the CLI self-update integration test environment on Windows platforms.

eli5.text: When you install this tool on Windows using a shell program called Git Bash, the installer would fail and show a confusing message about a 'remote tape address' instead of unpacking the files correctly. That happened because Git Bash comes with its own version of a file-unpacking program that misread Windows-style folder paths, so the installer now tells the computer to use Windows' built-in unpacking tool instead. This only affects people who run the automated test that checks the installer works after a new version is published; it does not change the tool itself or what you see in normal use. The fix is live today for anyone running that test on a Windows machine.

Inline agents replace the parent's history with their result. Track which current-step messages they inherited so finalization does not append them a second time. Object identity is local to this stream and never serialized.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question and it starts answering you a little bit at a time, you now have the ability to stop that response mid-stream instead of waiting for it to finish. This is handy if you asked something by accident, changed your mind, or the assistant is taking too long to respond. Behind the scenes, the system that sends your question to the AI now listens for a 'stop' signal, so your request can be cleanly cancelled while it's still working.

ai.title: Terminal isolation becomes a synchronous lease controller
ai.summary: Interactive hosts now pass a `terminalCommandIsolation` capability into `runTerminalCommand`, which acquires isolation synchronously before `spawn` and releases it only after the command's whole process group exits. The CLI's new `TerminalProtocolController` (replacing the former `windows-terminal-command-guard`) disables mouse and focus reporting during any active command lease, keeps focus detection live, and restores the protocols exactly once after the final process exits, while headless SDK consumers can omit the option entirely.

ai.title: Desktop failed turn recovery event added to always-track analytics
ai.summary: Analytics now unconditionally tracks `DESKTOP_FAILED_TURN_RECOVERY` in `common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts`. Low-volume recovery funnel requires full sampling to measure creation-to-success and repeated-failure rates. Covers shared core constants and sampling utility. Event added to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS` alongside `DESKTOP_TURN_STALLED` to prevent statistical gaps in reliability metrics.

eli5.text: Every time the desktop app tried to recover from a failed turn but kept failing, the system already recorded that moment, but it only counted a random sample of those events rather than all of them. Now the system records every single one of those failed-recovery events instead of just some, so reliability metrics won't have gaps. You wouldn't notice this directly, but it helps the developers measure how often failed turns succeed on a second try versus fail repeatedly.

ai.title: output-limit recovery handles normal stops after reasoning
ai.summary: Stream recovery logic now classifies 'output-limit' for streams ending with a normal stop after emitting only native reasoning, not just length-based stops. This prevents silent turn failures when models think without answering. Changes span SDK stream interruption detection, agent runtime tags, and common type contracts.

eli5.text: When an assistant thinks out loud but then stops without giving you an answer - whether it ran out of space while thinking, or just quietly stopped after reasoning - the system now treats that as a recoverable situation instead of silently failing. It will automatically take another attempt so you don't get stuck with an empty response. This matters only when the assistant's visible reply is completely missing, not when it gives you a partial answer.

facts: Signal completion before this process reaps its own group so the parent receives the result even when the shell left background descendants.
Normal cleanup belongs to this detached process. In particular, Windows taskkill must not block the parent CLI's renderer thread after every successful command.
A zombie-visible group or faulty broker can remain "alive" forever. Stop retaining it after a bounded post-kill observation window.
A process can exit while a descendant ignores SIGTERM. Preserve bounded escalation and tracking while cleanup is still active.
entries.title: CLI update: terminal-command-broker
entries.summary: CLI, SDK changes across 3 file(s) (+416/−92).

ai.title: Terminal broker performs bounded self-cleanup instead of waiting
ai.summary: The terminal command broker now reaps its own process group immediately after writing the protocol result, rather than waiting for the parent CLI to disconnect first, which prevents Windows taskkill from blocking the parent renderer thread after every successful command. defaultBrokerInvocation now resolves the CLI entrypoint via path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'entry.ts') instead of reading process.argv[1], and createTerminalCommandBroker accepts an injectable terminate function plus wraps spawn and pipe failures in brokerFailure with the new TERMINAL_COMMAND_BROKER_RECOVERY guidance. The SDK's direct spawn path replaced its infinite cleanup loop with the bounded waitForProcessExit helper (KILL_ESCALATION_MS) for both SIGTERM and SIGKILL, so detached background descendants from SYNC commands are reaped within a capped window instead of risking an infinite wait, and the abort/timeout path now finishes tracking after the same bounded post-kill observation.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts, the broker no longer waits for parentDisconnected before calling reapOwnProcessGroup() after writeProtocol; instead it immediately runs its own cleanup, and defaultBrokerInvocation now resolves its own entrypoint via path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'entry.ts') rather than process.argv[1]. In sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts, the infinite while-loop in spawnDirectTerminalCommand was replaced with the bounded waitForProcessExit helper, and the abort/timeout cleanup now stops tracking after a KILL_ESCALATION_MS post-kill window. In cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts, the broker-failure smoke path now constructs a real broker via createTerminalCommandBroker({ invocation }) that points at a missing exe and asserts the resulting 'Failed to start terminal command broker' / 'Restart Freebuff' guidance.
ai.unknowns: Whether the smoke-test harness fully exercises the new entrypoint resolution across non-binary and binary builds.

changes.what: Broker runs its own reapOwnProcessGroup immediately after writeProtocol instead of awaiting parentDisconnected, and broker startup/spawn failures are routed through brokerFailure with TERMINAL_COMMAND_BROKER_RECOVERY; defaultBrokerInvocation resolves entry.ts via import.meta.dir.

Direct spawn path uses bounded waitForProcessExit (KILL_ESCALATION_MS) for SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL escalation instead of an infinite loop, and abort/timeout cleanup stops tracking after the bounded post-kill window.
Broker-failure smoke path now builds a real broker with createTerminalCommandBroker pointing at a missing exe and asserts the Restart Freebuff recovery guidance.
